title: What auditors and reviewers found about child-care money
question: What have the Controller, the budget analyst, independent auditors and prosecutors put in writing about child-care subsidies and early-education spending in San Francisco?
finding: 9 official documents are on file. The Controller's 2019 audit found subsidies properly granted but 69 of 579 subsidised providers potentially over licensed capacity, and reported in 2022 that its recommendations were carried out. The school district's auditor could not find documents for 28 of 47 sampled child-care grant charges in fiscal 2022 (likely questioned costs $6,711,381). Federal audits of the three pass-through agencies report no findings in 21 audit years; among State contract holders, auditors reported findings at Glide Foundation, Compass Family Services, none of them on a child-care, Head Start or meal grant. One criminal case alleging payment for care not provided was charged in 2025 and is unresolved.
how: Every document in the project's files that an auditor, the Controller, the Budget and Legislative Analyst or a prosecutor issued about child-care or early-education money in San Francisco was read, and its central statement is given with the date and a link. Figures are taken from the documents' own text. Federal audit results are from the Federal Audit Clearinghouse file for each organization's tax number.
limits: An audit finding says a rule or control was not met; it is not a finding of fraud. A charge is an allegation, and the two people charged pleaded not guilty; they are not named here. A clean federal audit covers federal money only and tests samples. No civil grand jury report on early care, no Controller or budget-analyst audit of the Department of Early Childhood since 2022, and no State review of a San Francisco child-care contractor was found; California's error-rate reports on child-care payments are published only statewide. The two national rows are context and say nothing about any San Francisco organization.

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst

document.t: Performance audit of San Francisco's early care and education programs

rows.said: The audit put the City's early-care budget at $66.2 million, found at least $995,000 left unspent in one year, and said the Human Services Agency "has not ensured optimal financial performance" by Children's Council, its sole-source fiscal agent for about $34 million a year.

rows.publisher: San Francisco Controller, City Services Auditor

document.t: The Office of Early Care and Education should strengthen oversight of its contracted agencies

rows.said: All 91 sampled subsidies were properly granted, but the office did not review case files, and 69 of 579 subsidised providers (12 percent) "potentially had more children enrolled than the capacity allowed"; proof of residency was insufficient for 8 of 14 families tested at one agency.

rows.publisher: San Francisco Controller, City Services Auditor

document.t: Field follow-up of the 2019 audit of eligibility screening at the Office of Early Care and Education

rows.said: The Controller reported that all five recommendations of the 2019 audit had been implemented and closed, including quarterly checks of provider capacity by the two agencies.

rows.publisher: Federal Audit Clearinghouse (independent auditor of the San Francisco Unified School District)

document.t: Single audit for fiscal 2022, findings 2022-008 and 2022-010 on the federal child-care grant

rows.said: The district could not document 28 of 47 sampled charges to the federal child-care grant (questioned costs of $39,372 known and $6,711,381 likely) and had no written procedure for identifying and recovering fraudulent child-care payments; both findings were graded material weaknesses.

document.t: Charges announced in a housing-benefit and child-care subsidy case

rows.said: Two people were charged with collecting over $30,000 a month in child-care subsidies through a nonprofit contractor for care that investigators say was not provided, for as many as 17 children; both pleaded not guilty and no outcome is on file.

document.t: Single audits of the three pass-through agencies, 2019 to 2025

rows.said: Independent auditors reported no findings in any of the 21 yearly federal audits of Children's Council, Wu Yee Children's Services and the Low Income Investment Fund.

document.t: Citywide nonprofit monitoring programme, fiscal 2025 results

rows.said: City fiscal monitoring of Children's Council recorded 6 findings in fiscal 2025, 1 still open at the end of the review (invoices).

rows.publisher: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Office of Inspector General

document.t: Meal reimbursement claims process for child-care centres (national audit 27601-0004-31)

rows.said: A national audit, not about San Francisco, found meal-count discrepancies at four of five sponsoring organizations it tested in one State and $6,672,035 of unsupported claims, and said capping claims at licensed capacity reduces inflated claims.

rows.publisher: U.S. Office of Management and Budget, PaymentAccuracy.gov

document.t: Child Care and Development Fund: improper payment rate

rows.said: Nationally the federal child-care grant was reported 95.1 percent accurate for fiscal 2025; no rate is published for California or for San Francisco.
